mainTopic: The burned פרים and שעירים: when their carriers become טמא, where they are burned (בירה and the three בית הדשן), and whether לינה, early יציאה, or a partial exit disqualifies them
overview: The משנה finishes the laws of the burned פרים and שעירים. The כהנים carry them out on poles, and each carrier's clothes become טמא once he passes the wall of the עזרה. רבי שמעון holds that only the burners become טמא, once the fire has caught most of the offering, and once the meat is fully scorched no one becomes טמא at all. The גמרא then explains the word בירה: רבי יוחנן says it is one spot on the הר הבית, while ריש לקיש says it is a name for the whole בית המקדש. Two versions follow of the three בית הדשן, the places of ashes: one in the עזרה, one on the הר הבית, and one outside the three מחנות. רבי ירמיה asks whether לינה disqualifies the burned bulls and goats, and every proof brought is pushed off. רבי אלעזר asks the same about leaving the עזרה too early, and that proof from לוי is pushed off too. Finally, רבי אלעזר asks how a small part of a limb is counted when about half the animal has gone out, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Carriers' clothing becomes impure once they leave the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים carry the burned offerings on poles. The ones in front become טמא in their clothes once they leave the wall of the עזרה; the ones behind only once they also leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would carry it on poles. If the front carriers went out past the wall of the courtyard and the back carriers did not yet go out, the front ones make their clothes impure, and the back ones do not make their clothes impure until they go out. Once both groups have gone out, they all make their clothes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה (according to the תנא קמא) explains exactly when the כהנים carrying the burned פרים and שעירים get their clothes made טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key moment is leaving the wall of the עזרה. It depends on where each person is, not on the offering as a whole. So the front carriers can be טמא while the back carriers, still inside, are not.

keyTerms.meaning: carrying (a heavy load)
poles
the wall of the Temple courtyard
make their clothes ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: This is about the carriers' clothes becoming טמא, not about the offering being disqualified. The offering is supposed to go out; that is its proper burning.

phrases.english: They would carry it on poles.
phrases.notes: "It" means the פרים and שעירים that get burned, which the משנה was just talking about.

phrases.english: If the first ones went out beyond the wall of the courtyard
and the latter ones did not go out —
the first ones make their clothes impure,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִים אֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין בְּגָדִים עַד שֶׁיָּצְאוּ.
phrases.english: and the latter ones do not make their clothes impure until they go out.
Once both these and those went out, they make their clothes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage; continues the משנה's discussion of the burned offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each carrier's clothes become טמא once he personally exits the wall of the עזרה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: impurity starts only when the fire catches most of it
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees: the carriers' clothes do not become טמא. The burners' clothes become טמא only once the fire has caught most of the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: They do not make clothes impure until the fire has taken hold of most of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues with the תנא קמא about when the clothes become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, even the carriers become טמא once they pass the עזרה wall. For רבי שמעון, the carriers do not become טמא at all. Only those who burn the offering do, and only once the fire has caught most of it.

keyTerms.meaning: that the fire is lit / catches
the majority of them

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: They do not make impure
until the fire has caught in the majority of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the תנא קמא's timing in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the clothes become טמא only once the fire has caught most of the offering.

steps.title: Once the meat is scorched, the burner is no longer affected
steps.stepSummary: If the meat has already been completely scorched, the one who burns it does not make his clothes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the meat has been fully scorched, the one who burns it does not make his clothes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an ending point: once the meat is scorched through, the טומאה of the clothes no longer applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1 and 2 told us when the טומאה starts. This line tells us when it stops: once the meat is no longer really meat but scorched remains, burning it does not make clothes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: scorched / melted down completely
the one who burns

steps.whatToRemember: There is a window for this טומאה: it starts when the carrier leaves the עזרה (or, for רבי שמעון, when the fire catches most of it), and it ends once the meat is fully scorched.

phrases.aramaic: נִיתַּךְ הַבָּשָׂר – אֵין הַשּׂוֹרֵף מְטַמֵּא בְּגָדִים.
phrases.english: If the meat was scorched — the one who burns does not make his clothes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the end point of the טומאה discussed in steps 1–2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning meat that is already completely scorched does not make the burner's clothes טמא.

steps.title: What is the בירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the word בירה, used earlier in the משנה, means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the בירה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the meaning of a word from the משנה. This is a setup line; the answers come in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה earlier said disqualified burned offerings are burned in the בירה. The גמרא wants to know exactly what place that is.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
what is
a place name connected to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the "bira"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the משנה to the גמרא, returning to a word from earlier in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning and location of the בירה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a specific spot on the Temple Mount
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the בירה is a particular place on the הר הבית that was named בירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: There is a place on the הר הבית, and its name is בירה.
steps.whatsHappening: First answer: the בירה is one specific spot on the הר הבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, בירה is a local place name, not a general word. So the burning happens at that particular location on the הר הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: the Temple Mount
its name

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם יֵשׁ בְּהַר הַבַּיִת, וּ״בִירָה״ שְׁמוֹ.
phrases.english: There is a place on the Temple Mount, and its name is "bira."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בירה is a specific place on the הר הבית that carries that name.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the whole Temple is called בירה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the entire בית המקדש is called בירה, and brings a פסוק that uses the word that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: The entire בית המקדש is called בירה, as it says: "the בירה for which I have prepared."
steps.whatsHappening: Second answer: בירה is not one spot but a name for the whole בית המקדש, supported by a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש shows from דוד's words about building the בית המקדש that the whole building is called בירה. This disagrees with רבי יוחנן, who held it is just one location on the הר הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: the entire Temple
as it is said (introducing a פסוק)
I have prepared

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
The entire Temple is called "bira,"
as it says: "the bira for which I have prepared."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 29:19. The word in round brackets appears in some versions and is left out in others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing answer to step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בירה is a name for the whole בית המקדש, as shown by the פסוק.

steps.title: Three ash places; the first is in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says there were three בית הדשן. The big one in the עזרה was for disqualified קדשי קדשים, disqualified אימורים of קדשים קלים, and burned פרים and שעירים disqualified before זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: There are three places of ashes. There was a great place of ashes in the עזרה, where they burn disqualified קדשי קדשים, the אימורים of קדשים קלים, and the burned bulls and burned goats that became disqualified before the זריקה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: there were three separate places of ashes, and the גמרא starts with the first one, inside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things that became פסול while still fully belonging to the inner holiness are burned right inside the עזרה. This includes the burned פרים and שעירים only if they became פסול before their blood was sprinkled.

keyTerms.meaning: place of the ashes (where things were burned)
disqualified offerings of the most holy kind
the altar portions of offerings of lighter holiness
the bulls and goats that are burned (not eaten)
sprinkling of the blood on the altar

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
There are three places of ashes:
There was a great place of ashes in the courtyard —
where they burn disqualified offerings of the most holy kind,
and the altar portions of offerings of lighter holiness,
phrases.notes: He means these portions when they became disqualified.

phrases.english: and burned bulls and burned goats
that became disqualified before the sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching about burning locations, related to the question of where the בירה is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three בית הדשן; the first, in the עזרה, is for things disqualified before זריקה (and disqualified קדשי קדשים and אימורים).

steps.title: The second ash place, on the Temple Mount
steps.stepSummary: The second בית הדשן was on the הר הבית, for burned פרים and שעירים that became פסול after זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was another place of ashes on the Temple Mount, where they burn the burned bulls and burned goats that became disqualified after the sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list with the second place of ashes, on the הר הבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dividing line is the זריקה. A burned פר or שעיר disqualified before זריקה is burned in the עזרה. One disqualified after זריקה is burned outside the עזרה, on the הר הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: that a disqualification happened to them
after the sprinkling

steps.confusionAlert: Both the first and second places handle burned פרים and שעירים. The only difference is whether the disqualification happened before or after the זריקה.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הַדֶּשֶׁן אַחֵר הָיָה בְּהַר הַבַּיִת –
phrases.english: And there was another place of ashes on the Temple Mount —
where they burn burned bulls
and burned goats
that became disqualified after the sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הַדֶּשֶׁן אַחֵר הָיָה בְּהַר הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of three from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burned פרים and שעירים disqualified after זריקה are burned in the בית הדשן on the הר הבית.

steps.title: The third ash place, outside the three camps
steps.stepSummary: The third place is for burned פרים and שעירים done properly: they are burned outside all three מחנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when done according to their מצוה, outside the three camps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list of three: valid burned offerings are burned outside the three מחנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two places are for disqualified offerings. When nothing went wrong, the פרים and שעירים are burned in their proper place, outside all three מחנות.

keyTerms.meaning: according to their מצוה (done properly)
the three camps

steps.whatToRemember: Three בית הדשן: (1) in the עזרה, for things disqualified before זריקה; (2) on the הר הבית, for burned פרים and שעירים disqualified after זריקה; (3) outside the three מחנות, for burned פרים and שעירים done properly.

phrases.english: And when done according to their מצוה, outside the three camps.
phrases.notes: This is the third place in the list, for the burned פרים and שעירים when nothing went wrong.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of three begun in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Properly offered burned פרים and שעירים are burned outside the three מחנות.

steps.title: Levi's version of the three places of ashes
steps.stepSummary: לוי teaches a different version. The great בית הדשן in the עזרה took disqualified פרים and שעירים whether the problem came before or after זריקה. The one on the הר הבית took those that became פסול when they left the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי taught: There are three places of ashes. A great place of ashes was in the עזרה. There they burned disqualified קדשי קדשים, the אימורים of קדשים קלים, and פרים and שעירים that are burned if they became disqualified, whether before זריקה or after זריקה. Another place of ashes was on the הר הבית. There they burned פרים and שעירים that became disqualified when they went out. And the ones done the proper way are burned outside the three מחנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings לוי's version of the same list of three places of ashes. It splits the cases a little differently from the version we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier version, only problems before זריקה went to the עזרה, and problems after זריקה went to the הר הבית. In לוי's version, the עזרה takes both before and after זריקה. The הר הבית place is only for animals that became פסול as they were being carried out. The third place, outside the three מחנות, is the same in both versions.

keyTerms.meaning: Place of ashes, where things are burned
A disqualification
When they went out (of the עזרה)
Done the proper way, as commanded

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new list. It is the same three places as steps 7-9. The only change is which disqualified פרים and שעירים go to the first place and which go to the second.

phrases.english: Levi teaches:
There are three places of ashes:
A great place of ashes was in the Temple courtyard,
where they burn disqualified offerings of the most holy kind,
and the altar parts of offerings of lesser holiness,
and bulls that are burned and goats that are burned
that became disqualified,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין קוֹדֶם זְרִיקָה בֵּין לְאַחַר זְרִיקָה.
phrases.english: whether before the sprinkling or after the sprinkling.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הַדֶּשֶׁן אַחֵר הָיָה בְּהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: And another place of ashes was on the Temple Mount,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁשָּׁם שׂוֹרְפִין פָּרִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִין וּשְׂעִירִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִין
phrases.english: where they burn bulls that are burned and goats that are burned
that became disqualified as they were going out.
And when done properly, they are burned outside the three camps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the list from steps 7-9, with a different split for disqualified פרים and שעירים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עזרה place takes disqualified פרים and שעירים whether the problem came before or after זריקה. The הר הבית place takes those disqualified on the way out. Proper ones are burned outside the three מחנות.

steps.title: Does leaving overnight disqualify the burned bulls and goats?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether לינה disqualifies פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים, since they are never eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: Does being left overnight disqualify the bulls and goats that are burned? Do we say that לינה only works on meat that is meant to be eaten, so it does not work on these, which are not eaten? Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה raises a new question. Does the rule that leftover meat becomes פסול overnight also apply to the bulls and goats that are burned?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, holy meat that sits past its time becomes פסול through לינה. The meat of these bulls and goats is not eaten by people and not burned on the מזבח, so maybe that rule does not apply to it. The other side of the question is that maybe לינה disqualifies any קדשים, eaten or not.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks / raises a question
Being left overnight, which disqualifies holy meat
Fit to be eaten
Or maybe there is no difference

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
What is the law: does being left overnight take effect
on bulls that are burned and goats that are burned?
Do we say: when being left overnight takes effect,
it is on meat that is meant to be eaten,
phrases.notes: Eaten here means by people or by the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָנֵי דְּלָאו בְּנֵי אֲכִילָה נִינְהוּ – לָא;
phrases.english: but these, which are not meant to be eaten, no;
or maybe there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the places of burning to a new question about the burned bulls and goats.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether לינה disqualifies offerings that are not eaten, like פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים.

steps.title: רבא's proof that לינה does not disqualify them
steps.stepSummary: רבא says אביי asked this too, and he answered it. Everyone agrees a bad intention about eating or burning the bulls does nothing, so לינה should also do nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: אביי asked this very question, and I answered him from this: Everyone agrees that if the כהן intended to eat or burn the bulls past their time, he did nothing. Isn't it so that since intention does not disqualify them, לינה also does not disqualify them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to answer רבי ירמיה's question using a known rule about intention (מחשבה). He compares the two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wrong intention, like planning to eat it after its time, usually makes an offering פיגול. Both sides of a known disagreement agree this does nothing to the burned bulls, because they are not eaten. רבא reasons that לינה works the same way, so it should not disqualify them either.

keyTerms.meaning: I resolved it for him
And they agree
He intended (had a thought during the service)
Intention, which can make an offering פסול
What, is it not so that... (introduces the proof)

phrases.english: Rava said:
This matter was asked by Abaye,
and I resolved it for him from this:
And they agree that if he intended
phrases.notes: 'They' are the two sides arguing about פיגול in these bulls, and on this point they agree.

phrases.english: about eating the bulls or burning them past their time,
he did nothing.
What, is it not that since intention does not disqualify them,
being left overnight also does not disqualify them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָא מִילְּתָא אִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְאַבָּיֵי, וּפְשַׁטְנָא לֵיהּ מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.raayaObject: That לינה does not disqualify פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreed rule that intending to eat or burn the bulls past their time does nothing.

steps.title: Intention and overnight may be different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe only intention fails to disqualify these offerings, while לינה still does.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it is only intention that does not disqualify them, while being left overnight does disqualify them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof. It says the two rules might not work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed that intention and לינה follow the same logic. The גמרא says that is not proven. Intention may only matter for things that are eaten, while לינה might disqualify any קדשים, so the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces a rejection)
Disqualifies

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה's question about לינה in burned bulls and goats is not settled by the rule about מחשבה, because the two rules may work differently.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is intention that does not disqualify,
but being left overnight does disqualify!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between מחשבה and לינה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes intention and לינה work the same way, but they may not.

steps.title: A משנה lists לינה as disqualifying burned bulls and goats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה saying that once פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים are slaughtered, they can become פסול through טבול יום, מחוסר כיפורים, and לינה. It suggests this means the meat itself becomes פסול through לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Bulls that are burned and goats that are burned — one is liable for מעילה with them from the time they were made holy. Once they are slaughtered, they can become פסול through a טבול יום, through a מחוסר כיפורים, and through being left overnight. Doesn't this mean the meat left overnight?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof for רבי ירמיה's question. It points to a משנה that lists לינה as one of the things that disqualify these burned offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in Step 12 failed because bad intention and לינה might work differently. Here the גמרא finds a source that names לינה directly. If the משנה is talking about the meat, then לינה clearly disqualifies the meat of these offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for מעילה, misusing something that belongs to the Temple
Someone who went to the מקוה today but must wait until nightfall to be fully טהור
Someone who finished becoming טהור but has not yet brought his required קרבן
Being left overnight, past the time limit

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Bulls that are burned and goats that are burned —
one is liable for misusing them from the time they were made holy.
Once they were slaughtered, they became able to be disqualified
through one who immersed today, through one still missing his atonement offering, and through being left overnight.
phrases.notes: The first two are people whose touch makes the offering פסול, even though they are not fully טמא.

phrases.english: What, is it not the meat being left overnight?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in Step 12 was pushed off, the גמרא tries a new source for רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's question: does לינה disqualify the meat of פרים ושעירים הנשרפים?
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (in מסכת מעילה) listing לינה among the things that disqualify these offerings after שחיטה.

steps.title: The משנה may mean the אימורין, not the meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the לינה in the משנה may refer to the אימורין, the parts that go on the מזבח, not to the meat that gets burned outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means the אימורין being left overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The משנה could be talking about a different part of the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These offerings have two parts: the אימורין, which are burned on the מזבח, and the meat, which is burned outside the camp. The אימורין have a set time on the מזבח, so לינה surely applies to them. That says nothing about the meat, which is what רבי ירמיה asked about.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
The meat — here, the part burned outside the camp

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two burnings: the אימורין are burned on the מזבח, while the rest of the meat is burned outside. רבי ירמיה's question is only about the meat.

phrases.english: No, it means the altar parts being left overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 14 by reading the משנה's לינה as being about the אימורין.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading that the משנה means the meat; it does not decide the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה's לינה is about the meat, but it may be about the אימורין.

steps.title: The end of the משנה talks about meat, so the beginning should too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the end of the same משנה says one is liable for מעילה in the בית הדשן until the meat is fully burned. Since the end is about meat, the beginning should be about meat too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the end of the משנה teaches: 'For all of them, one is liable for מעילה in the בית הדשן until the meat is completely burned' — since the end is about meat, the beginning is also about meat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 15. It uses the end of the same משנה to show the משנה is talking about meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that one משנה usually stays on the same subject. The end clearly talks about the meat being burned in the בית הדשן. So the לינה at the beginning should also be about the meat, which would bring back the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a משנה or ברייתא
The beginning part of a משנה or ברייתא
Until it is completely burned up

phrases.english: But since the end of the משנה teaches:
For all of them, one is liable for misusing them in the place of the ashes
until the meat is completely burned up —
since the end is about meat, the beginning is also about meat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 15 and tries to bring back the proof of Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה's לינה means the אימורין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה is about meat, so the beginning should also be about meat.

steps.title: The two parts of the משנה can be about different things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this doesn't follow: the end can be about meat while the beginning is about אימורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a reason?! The end is about meat, and the beginning is about אימורין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer. It says a משנה can switch subjects between its beginning and its end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no rule that the beginning and end must be about the same part of the animal. Each clause can be about whatever fits it best. So the answer in Step 15 stands, and the proof from this משנה fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a reason? — the cases are not the same, so you can't learn one from the other

phrases.english: Is that a reason?!
The end is about meat, and the beginning is about the altar parts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16 and keeps the answer of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the משנה: each clause is about a different part of the animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה must be about the same thing, so the beginning is about meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end is about meat and the beginning is about אימורין, so the משנה does not prove לינה disqualifies the meat.

steps.title: A proof from לוי's teaching about offerings that became פסול when going out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings לוי's teaching that the בית הדשן on the הר הבית received offerings that became פסול when they went out. It suggests this means they became פסול through לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what לוי teaches: 'Those that became פסול when they went out.' Doesn't this mean through לינה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more proof for רבי ירמיה's question, using לוי's teaching from Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי said the second בית הדשן received offerings that became פסול on their way out of the עזרה. The גמרא suggests this happened because the trip took too long and they were left overnight. If so, לינה does disqualify the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: When they went out (of the עזרה)
Something happened to them that made them פסול

phrases.english: Come and hear, for לוי teaches:
those that became disqualified when they went out.
What, is it not through being left overnight?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה failed, the גמרא tries לוי's teaching instead.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's question about לינה for the meat of פרים ושעירים הנשרפים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: לוי's teaching about offerings that became פסול when they went out of the עזרה.

steps.title: לוי meant טומאה or leaving too early, not לינה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that לוי's 'פסול when going out' means they became טמא, or they went out before the זריקה. It does not have to mean לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means becoming פסול through טומאה, or becoming פסול through going out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off this last proof. לוי's words can be explained without לינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are other ways an offering can become פסול on its way out: it can become טמא, or it can be taken out of the עזרה too early, before the blood was sprinkled. Since לוי's teaching fits these, it does not prove that לינה disqualifies the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Becoming פסול because it became טמא
Becoming פסול because it left its proper area too early

steps.whatToRemember: Every proof for רבי ירמיה's question was pushed off: the משנה can mean the אימורין, and לוי can mean טומאה or יציאה. So far, nothing settles whether לינה disqualifies the meat of פרים ושעירים הנשרפים.

phrases.english: No, it means disqualified through impurity, and disqualified through going out.
phrases.notes: Going out here means leaving the עזרה before the blood was sprinkled, which makes the offering פסול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 18 by explaining לוי's words a different way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof; the question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'פסול when going out' means לינה, but it can mean טומאה or going out too early.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks whether going out makes the burned bulls and goats פסול
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks whether יציאה, leaving the עזרה, makes פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: does going out of the עזרה make the bulls that are burned and the goats that are burned פסול?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי אלעזר asks whether the normal rule of יציאה, that meat taken out of the עזרה becomes פסול, also applies to פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, meat of a קרבן that leaves the עזרה becomes פסול. But these special bulls and goats are supposed to be taken outside and burned there. So it is not clear whether going out can make them פסול at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question that has no clear answer yet
Going out of the עזרה, which normally makes קדשים פסול
Bulls whose meat is burned outside instead of being eaten
Goats whose meat is burned outside instead of being eaten

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked:
Going out, does it take effect
phrases.notes: Literally 'does it help.' He means: does going out work to make these offerings פסול?

phrases.english: for bulls that are burned
and goats that are burned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about פרים הנשרפים, connected to the earlier discussion of offerings burned in the בית הדשן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does יציאה make פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים פסול?

steps.title: Why is this even a question?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אלעזר is unsure about, since these offerings are burned outside anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly is he asking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by רבי אלעזר's question and asks what the doubt could be. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat of these offerings has to be taken out and burned outside, so going out seems like a normal part of what happens to them. How could going out make them פסול? The גמרא wants to know what situation רבי אלעזר has in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he unsure about? A question asking what a doubt is based on

phrases.english: What is he unsure about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the question in Step 20 is a real question at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what situation could going out make offerings פסול when they are meant to go out?

steps.title: The question follows the view that leaving too early is a problem
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא explains that the question follows the view that meat which leaves before its time becomes פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: the question follows the person who says that meat which goes out too early is פסול, because its time to go out has not yet come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה בר אבא answers the גמרא's puzzle. רבי אלעזר is asking according to the view that leaving too early, before the זריקה, makes meat פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a view that even קדשים קלים, which may be eaten anywhere in ירושלים, become פסול if they leave the עזרה before the זריקה, because 'its time has not yet come.' The question is whether this idea of leaving too early also applies to the burned bulls and goats, whose meat leaves only after the זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
Its time has not yet come
Throwing the blood on the מזבח, the step that makes the meat allowed
Offerings of lesser holiness, which may be eaten anywhere in ירושלים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
according to the one who says
its time to go out has not yet come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by explaining which view the question is based on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is about meat leaving before its proper time, according to the view that leaving too early makes it פסול.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the 'too early' rule only applies to meat that never has to leave, or maybe it applies to the burned bulls and goats too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that this rule only applies to meat that does not have to go out, but these, which must go out in the end, are not made פסול? Or maybe here too, its time to go out has not yet come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out both sides of רבי אלעזר's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the 'too early' rule only applies to ordinary meat, which never has to leave, so these bulls and goats, which must leave in the end, are not made פסול. Side two: early is still early, so if they leave before their time, they are פסול too.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we say? This opens the first side of a question
This rule applies only to
It will have to go out in the end
Something that must be done
Or maybe. This opens the second side of a question

phrases.english: Do we say:
this applies only to meat
that does not have to go out in the end,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָנֵי דְּסוֹפָן לָצֵאת חוֹבָה – לָא;
phrases.english: but these, which must go out in the end, are not;
or maybe here too
its time to go out has not come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 22 by laying out the two possible answers to the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the 'too early' rule depend on the meat never having to leave, or does it apply to any meat that leaves before its time?

steps.title: Trying to prove it from לוי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that לוי's phrase 'became פסול when going out' means they became פסול by going out too early.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what לוי taught: offerings that became פסול when they went out. Doesn't this mean they became פסול by going out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבי אלעזר's question with לוי's teaching about the בית הדשן on the הר הבית. That place was for burned bulls and goats that became פסול 'when going out.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'when going out' means the going out itself made them פסול, then early going out does make these bulls and goats פסול. That would answer the question with side two.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that makes a קרבן unfit
Doesn't it mean? This suggests a reading of a source

steps.confusionAlert: לוי's teaching was already used in Step 18 to try to prove a לינה point. Here the same words are used for a different question, about יציאה.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for לוי taught:
that it became פסול when it went out.
What, doesn't it mean it was made פסול by going out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question in Step 23 using לוי's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: Going out too early makes פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: לוי's teaching: offerings that became פסול when going out were burned in the בית הדשן on the הר הבית.

steps.title: No, it means טומאה or לינה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: לוי may mean they became פסול through טומאה or לינה, not through going out.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means they were made פסול by טומאה, or made פסול by לינה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'When going out' only tells us when the problem happened, not that going out caused it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offerings could have become טמא, or stayed overnight (לינה), and then been burned at the בית הדשן on the הר הבית. So לוי's teaching tells us nothing about יציאה, and רבי אלעזר's question stays unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: Becoming פסול because it was left overnight

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר asked whether leaving the עזרה too early makes the burned bulls and goats פסול, since they must go out in the end anyway. The proof from לוי was pushed away, because 'פסול when going out' can mean טומאה or לינה. The question is left unanswered.

phrases.english: No; made פסול by impurity
or made פסול by being left overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 24 by reading לוי's words differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from לוי. The question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'פסול when going out' does not have to mean פסול caused by going out. It can mean טומאה or לינה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעזר's question about יציאה for פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים remains unanswered.

steps.title: Does a small piece of a limb follow its limb or the whole animal?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks about a burned bull or goat where most of the animal went out of the עזרה, but only by counting a small piece of a limb whose larger part stayed inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: burned bulls and burned goats, where most of the animal went out, but only by counting a small part of a limb, what is the law? Does that small part of the limb follow the majority of its own limb, and that majority did not go out? Or does it follow the majority of the animal?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר opens a new question. He asks whether the animal counts as having gone out when 'most of it' is outside only because a small piece of a limb is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to count that small piece. If it follows its own limb, it counts as 'inside', because most of the limb is still inside, so most of the animal is not out. If it follows the whole animal, it counts as 'outside', and most of the animal is out.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question (a real open question, not an attack)
The bulls and goats whose bodies are burned outside instead of being eaten
A small part (minority) of a limb
We 'throw it after the majority': the smaller part takes the status of the larger part
Or perhaps (introduces the second side of the question)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked:
Bulls that are burned and goats that are burned,
where most of them went out
phrases.notes: Some versions say רוּבּוֹ, 'most of it'; the wording in square brackets is רוּבָּן, 'most of them.' The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: by means of a small part of a limb, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The animal only reaches 'most of it outside' by counting that small piece of the limb.

phrases.english: This small part of the limb,
do we treat it as following the majority [of its limb],
and that [majority of the limb] did not go out?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, בָּתַר רוּבָּא דִּבְהֵמָה שָׁדֵינַן?
phrases.english: Or perhaps we treat it as following the majority of the animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question by רבי אלעזר after the discussion of לוי's words ended with a rejected proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a small part of a limb, whose larger part is still inside, count with its own limb or with the majority of the animal when deciding whether most of the animal went out?

steps.title: Obviously we follow the majority of the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the question as worded is obvious: we would never ignore the majority of the whole animal and follow the majority of a limb instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that we do not leave aside the majority of the animal and follow the majority of the limbs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רבי אלעזר's question was worded. It says one side is clearly right, so there is nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole animal is the main thing being judged, so its majority should decide. Judging by the majority of one limb, against the majority of the whole animal, makes no sense. So the case must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (used to argue that a question or statement is not needed)
We leave aside / ignore
We go after / follow

phrases.english: It is obvious that we do not leave aside
the majority of the animal
and follow the majority of the limbs!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the question in step 26 as having an obvious answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי אלעזר's question in step 26
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The majority of the whole animal clearly outweighs the majority of a single limb, so the second side of the question is obviously right and there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: Rewording the question: half the animal went out with most of a limb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רבי אלעזר's question: exactly half of the animal went out, together with most of one limb. It begins to ask how the small part of that limb left inside is counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where half of it went out, with most of a limb. This small part of the limb that stayed inside...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the question so it is no longer obvious. Now exactly half the animal is out, and most of one limb is out too. The rest of the question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With exactly half outside, the whole animal has no majority either way, so the limb's status can decide the case. Most of the limb went out, but a small piece of it is still inside. The question will be whether that inside piece follows its own limb and counts as 'out', which would make most of the animal out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected version of the case)
Half of it
Most of a limb

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the case has flipped. Before, a small piece outside was being added to reach a majority. Now, most of the limb is outside, and the question is about the small piece left inside.

phrases.english: Rather, [the case is] where half of it went out, along with most of a limb:
this small part of the limb [that stayed inside]...
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the question about this piece is finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 27 by restating רבי אלעזר's question as a case that is not obvious.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about a small piece outside being added to reach a majority of the animal, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about a case where exactly half the animal is out, so the status of the small piece of the limb left inside decides whether most of the animal is out.
